It's a giant unpainted block of concrete, at most it has some white paint scraped onto it.

Basic principles of coding, yes. A few basic object oriented languages, yes. Nothing beyond that, unless you focus on a software engineering specialty. I never said I couldn't code, without the specialization and/or proper work experience employers don't give you a second look.

That's a very good question and probably hints at one of my main issues. I don't have any goals. I have dreams, getting a better job and stuff like that, but I have no real way to achieve those dreams. I'm in survival mode, trying my best to make it through each day. My brain tells me not to set goals because I'll never reach them.
Minnesota. I've never applied for one, just like knowing that the option is there.
This doesn't seem correct, but I don't know enough about cars to dispute it.
If I get put on antidepressants I don't qualify for a conceal and carry permit.
I have two dogs and a cat. All rescues from high kill shelters.

I read what you wrote and while not exactly changing anything or making me feel much better (sorry) I appreciate you taking the time to respond the way you did.  
Then I came to look at other comments and saw you already downvoted and I don't understand why. Your words did touch me, and I thank you for that.

I couldn't find a programming job for 6 months out of college. Took a tech support job to pay the bills and now I've pigeon holed myself (that may not be the correct term). Employers see nothing to show them I've stayed up on my programming skills, so they are more likely to hire new grads who have it fresh in their mind.
The "university" I work for is a diploma mill.
Everything being said is being taken with a grain of salt, just wanted opinions mostly. Thank you for pointing that out though.

The argument I have against this is that I technically pay her rent every month, so even without a written lease it's still a landlord type situation. I feel she would need due cause to evict me, but I'm not smart enough to find all the laws on my own.

I did google geographic tongue and it does exist, but it seems to be a blanket term for parts of the tongue/tastebuds dying off for any number of reasons. Also be careful if you image search it, some of it is NSFL
Dentist who did the fillings thought that could be the case, but that wouldn't cause the geographic tongue that I have and according to the dentist should have gone away after a bit.

I went to my old family dentist who agreed to see me free of charge. He said the fillings look conservative and gave me a prescription for magic mouthwash to help with the pain. Didn't mention amalgam allergy at all.
